Articulation Agreement Overview

This agreement outlines lower-division course requirements specific to the major. Students are strongly encouraged to consult an academic advisor to ensure they meet all degree requirements for their intended baccalaureate program.


Helpful Resources:

  • CSUB Catalog
  • Transfer Admission Requirements
  • Academic Advising Student Centers
  • CSUB Program Pathways Mapper


Course Equivalency Information for 4-Year Institutions

Students and staff can explore course transfer equivalencies through the Transfer Evaluation System (TES). Equivalency agreements are updated regularly and subject to change. For the most current information, please refer to TES or contact the Articulation Office.

notes.content: The Department of Biology offers the Bachelor of Science in Biology with or without a concentration in Biotechnology, the Bachelor of Arts in Human Biological Sciences, and the Master of Science in Biology. Throughout its curriculum, the Department emphasizes evolution and the relationship between organisms and the environment. Classes include extensive field and laboratory investigations allowing students to observe and measure biological systems. Students are encouraged to select elective courses best suited to their interests. For additional information, visit the following: Department of Biology Program Requirements - Biology, BS, Concentration in Biotechnology

notes.content: Students who have taken Biology or Chemistry coursework should check the Articulation Agreement by the Department of the respective community colleges. The agreement may articulate differently, and it may determine whether the entire Biology and/or Chemistry sequence needs to be completed to receive appropriate course credit for the major requirements at CSUB. A modification to the standard GE program has been approved that allows the possibility of satisfying some GE requirements through the major. BIOL 2010 or BIOL 2110 satisfies B2, MATH 1050 or higher satisfies B4, and CHEM 1000 satisfies B1.
